props.code:
def node(kind, label, group, ports, icon, doc, inputs=None, accent="neutral"):
    return {"kind": kind, "label": label, "group": group, "ports": ports,
            "icon": icon, "doc": doc, "accent": accent,
            "config_schema": inputs or {}}

return [
    node("start", "Start", "Flow", ["next"], "\u25b8",
         "Where the execution begins. Exactly one per playbook.",
         accent="flow"),
    node("end", "End", "Flow", [], "\u25a0",
         "A terminal outcome. A playbook may have several.",
         {"outcome": {"enum": ["succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"]}},
         accent="flow"),

    node("condition", "Condition", "Logic", ["then", "else"], "\u25c7",
         "Branch on a typed expression over the variables in scope. The expression is parsed into an AST, not evaluated as code.",
         {"expression": {"type": "string", "widget": "expression"}},
         accent="logic"),
    node("switch", "Switch", "Logic", ["case", "default"], "\u2442",
         "Multi-way branch on one value.",
         {"subject": {"type": "string", "widget": "variable"},
          "cases": {"type": "object", "widget": "case_map"}},
         accent="logic"),
    node("for_each", "For Each", "Logic", ["body", "next"], "\u21bb",
         "Bounded iteration. max_iterations is mandatory - the validator refuses an unbounded loop, because an unbounded loop in a SOAR is an outage.",
         {"items": {"type": "string", "widget": "variable"},
          "as": {"type": "string"},
          "max_iterations": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 10000,
                             "default": 100},
          "concurrency": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 20,
                          "default": 1}},
         accent="logic"),
    node("while", "While", "Logic", ["body", "next"], "\u27f3",
         "Repeat while a condition holds, up to max_iterations.",
         {"expression": {"type": "string", "widget": "expression"},
          "max_iterations": {"type": "integer", "default": 50}},
         accent="logic"),
    node("parallel", "Parallel", "Logic", ["branches", "next"], "\u2225",
         "Fan out and join. Join on all, any, or n of the branches.",
         {"join": {"enum": ["all", "any", "n"], "default": "all"},
          "n": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1}},
         accent="logic"),

    node("command", "Command", "Action", ["next", "on_error"], "\u25f0",
         "Run a command from the registry. Drag a specific command from the catalogue below instead of this generic node unless you intend to choose it at run time.",
         {"command": {"type": "string", "widget": "command_picker"}},
         accent="action"),
    node("response", "Response Action", "Action", ["next", "on_error",
                                                   "on_unsupported"], "\u25e4",
         "An ABSTRACT containment action - isolate a host, block a hash - resolved at run time against whichever EDR actually has an agent on that host. Use this rather than a vendor command when the estate has more than one EDR. The on_unsupported branch is where hosts whose EDR cannot perform the action go.",
         {"action": {"type": "string", "widget": "response_picker"},
          "target": {"type": "string", "widget": "variable"},
          "mode": {"type": "string", "widget": "mode_picker"}},
         accent="danger"),
    node("http", "HTTP Request", "Action", ["next", "on_error"], "\u25f9",
         "A one-off HTTP call. Destination is screened by the SSRF guard on the resolved address, and redirects are re-screened.",
         {"method": {"enum": ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"]},
          "url": {"type": "string"},
          "headers": {"type": "object"}, "body": {"type": "object"}},
         accent="action"),
    node("script", "Script", "Action", ["next", "on_error"], "\u007b\u007d",
         "Custom Python, for computing something no command covers. For "
         "rendering text or HTML use Format instead - this executes, that "
         "one templates. Runs in the sandbox pool: no network, no credentials, no filesystem beyond a tmpfs. Promote it to verified after review if it needs more.",
         {"source": {"type": "string", "widget": "code"},
          "trust_level": {"enum": ["untrusted", "verified"],
                          "default": "untrusted"}},
         accent="action"),
    node("format", "Format", "Data", ["next"], "\u25a5",
         "Render a template into text, HTML or markdown - an alert "
         "description, an email body, a ticket note. {{ path }} and "
         "{{ path | filter }} over the variables in scope, which is "
         "Jinja-SHAPED and deliberately not Jinja: this resolves paths "
         "and cannot call anything, because a template engine that can "
         "reach an object attribute is the cheapest remote code "
         "execution in this product class. Output is escaped for the "
         "format you pick.",
         {"template": {"type": "string", "widget": "code"},
          "format": {"enum": ["html", "text", "markdown"],
                     "default": "html"},
          "output_var": {"type": "string"}},
         accent="data"),
    node("sub_playbook", "Sub-Playbook", "Action", ["next", "on_error"],
         "\u29c9",
         "Invoke another published playbook. Cycles are refused at publish, at any depth.",
         {"playbook": {"type": "string", "widget": "playbook_picker"}},
         accent="action"),

    node("ai", "AI Action", "AI", ["next", "on_error"], "\u25c9",
         "One of the governed AI actions. Output is schema-validated; a malformed response fails the step rather than being coerced.",
         {"action": {"enum": ["analyze", "classify", "extract", "summarize",
                              "investigate", "recommend", "generate_query",
                              "mitre_map"]},
          "role": {"enum": ["fast", "investigation", "reasoning"],
                   "default": "fast"}},
         accent="ai"),

    node("approval", "Approval", "Control", ["on_approve", "on_reject",
                                            "on_timeout"], "\u229a",
         "Suspend until a human decides. A HIGH-risk approval cannot proceed on timeout - the option is not in the enum and the validator refuses it.",
         {"action_key": {"type": "string"},
          "risk_level": {"enum": ["low", "medium", "high"], "default": "high"},
          "summary": {"type": "string"},
          "timeout_s": {"type": "integer", "default": 1800},
          "on_timeout_behaviour": {"enum": ["reject", "escalate"],
                                   "default": "reject"}},
         accent="approval"),
    node("task", "Human Task", "Control", ["next"], "\u25a4",
         "Create a task for a person. Optionally wait for it.",
         {"title": {"type": "string"}, "detail": {"type": "string"},
          "assignee_role": {"type": "string"},
          "wait": {"type": "boolean", "default": False}},
         accent="approval"),
    node("delay", "Delay", "Control", ["next"], "\u25f4",
         "A durable wait - a scheduled wake, not a held thread or a worker.",
         {"seconds": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 604800}},
         accent="neutral"),

    node("set_var", "Set Variable", "Data", ["next"], "\u2261",
         "Assign into a declared scope.",
         {"name": {"type": "string"}, "value": {"type": "string",
                                                "widget": "variable"}},
         accent="data"),
    node("transform", "Transform", "Data", ["next"], "\u2234",
         "Reshape data with the same path syntax the mappings use. Pure: no side effects, runs in the scheduler.",
         {"mapping": {"type": "object", "widget": "mapping"}},
         accent="data"),
    node("incident_update", "Update Incident", "Data", ["next"], "\u25eb",
         "Change status, severity, assignment or tags, and write the timeline entry that goes with it.",
         {"status": {"type": "string"}, "severity": {"type": "string"},
          "note": {"type": "string"}, "tags": {"type": "array"}},
         accent="data"),
]

props.doc:
The palette for this principal.

Filtered by permission, and by what is actually installed. A command whose
integration is not configured appears greyed with the reason, rather than
being hidden - an engineer looking for "Isolate Host" and not finding it will
assume the platform cannot do it, which is worse than telling them CrowdStrike
is not connected yet.
props.name: build_palette

props.code:
from soar.identity.rbac import has_permission, require_permission
from soar.integrations.catalog import all_commands

require_permission(principal, "playbooks.read")
org_id = principal["org_id"]
held = principal.get("permissions") or []

installed = {row["connector_id"]: row for row in db.query(
    "SELECT connector_id, name, health, enabled FROM integration "
    "WHERE org_id = %s", [org_id], org_id,
)}

published = {row["key"]: row for row in db.query(
    "SELECT c.key, c.name, c.category, c.trust_level, c.integration_id, "
    "cv.input_schema, cv.output_schema, cv.risk_level, cv.effect, "
    "cv.required_permissions, cv.timeout_ms, cv.implementation "
    "FROM command c JOIN command_version cv ON cv.id = c.current_version_id "
    "WHERE (c.org_id = %s OR c.org_id IS NULL) AND NOT c.deprecated "
    "AND cv.state = 'published'", [org_id], org_id,
)}

groups = {}
for command in all_commands():
    key = command["key"]
    live = published.get(key)
    connector = installed.get(command["connector_id"])

    missing = []
    if connector is None:
        missing.append("%s is not configured" % command["connector_name"])
    elif not connector["enabled"]:
        missing.append("%s is disabled" % connector["name"])
    elif connector["health"] == "failing":
        missing.append("%s is failing its health check" % connector["name"])
    if live is None and connector is not None:
        missing.append("command is not published in this organisation")

    denied = [p for p in command["required_permissions"]
              if not has_permission(held, p)]

    entry = {
        "kind": "command",
        "command": key,
        "label": command["name"],
        "group": palette_group(command),
        "vendor": command["vendor"],
        "category": command["connector_category"],
        "risk_level": command["risk_level"],
        "effect": command["effect"],
        "undo": command.get("undo_command"),
        "doc": command.get("doc", ""),
        "config_schema": command["input_schema"],
        "outputs": command["output_schema"].get("properties", {}),
        "ports": ["next", "on_error"],
        "icon": "\u2699",
        "accent": "danger" if command["effect"] == "mutating" else "action",
        "available": not missing and not denied,
        "unavailable_reason": "; ".join(missing + [
            "you do not hold %s" % p for p in denied]),
        "requires_approval": command["risk_level"] == "high",
        "timeout_ms": command["timeout_ms"],
    }
    groups.setdefault(entry["group"], []).append(entry)

for entries in groups.values():
    entries.sort(key=lambda e: e["label"])

return {
    "core": core_nodes(),
    "commands": groups,
    "response_actions": response_action_palette(db, org_id),
    "variables": variable_roots(),
    "playbooks": db.query(
        "SELECT p.key, p.name, p.description FROM playbook p "
        "JOIN playbook_version pv ON pv.id = p.current_version_id "
        "WHERE p.org_id = %s AND pv.state = 'published' ORDER BY p.name",
        [org_id], org_id),
    "filters": palette_filters(),
}

props.doc:
The abstract response actions, each carrying its estate coverage.

This is the answer to "EDR response actions vary from EDR to EDR". The
analyst drags one node - Isolate Host - and the editor tells them, there and
then, which of their EDRs can do it, what each one means by it, and how much
of the estate is left uncovered. What they cannot do is draw a playbook that
looks like it contains every host and quietly does not.
props.name: response_action_palette

props.code:
from soar.integrations.catalog_edr import action_coverage

ACTIONS = [
    ("isolate_host", "Isolate Host", "high",
     "Take the endpoint off the network. What that means varies by EDR - see the per-vendor note below before relying on it."),
    ("release_host", "Release Host", "medium",
     "Lift containment. The declared compensation for Isolate Host."),
    ("restrict_execution", "Restrict Execution", "high",
     "Allow only signed binaries. Lighter than isolation; not every EDR has it."),
    ("block_hash", "Block File Hash", "high",
     "Estate-wide prevention for a file. A wrong hash blocks a legitimate binary everywhere at once."),
    ("quarantine_file", "Quarantine File", "high",
     "Remove the file on the endpoint."),
    ("scan_host", "Scan Host", "medium",
     "On-demand antimalware scan."),
    ("collect_evidence", "Collect Evidence", "medium",
     "Triage artefacts. Run this BEFORE remediation, not after."),
    ("kill_process", "Kill Process", "high",
     "Terminate a running process."),
    ("live_response", "Live Response", "high",
     "Interactive session on the endpoint."),
]

palette = []
for key, label, risk, doc in ACTIONS:
    coverage = action_coverage(db, org_id, key)
    palette.append({
        "kind": "response",
        "action": key,
        "label": label,
        "group": "Endpoint Response",
        "risk_level": risk,
        "effect": "mutating",
        "doc": doc,
        "icon": "\u26a1",
        "accent": "danger",
        "ports": ["next", "on_error", "on_unsupported"],
        "coverage": coverage,
        "available": coverage["hosts_covered"] > 0,
        "unavailable_reason": (
            "" if coverage["hosts_covered"] > 0
            else "no configured EDR implements %s" % key),
        "requires_approval": risk == "high",
        "warn": (
            "" if coverage["percent"] >= 99.0
            else "covers %.1f%% of hosts - wire the on_unsupported branch"
                 % coverage["percent"]),
        "config_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": ["target"],
            "properties": {
                "target": {"type": "string", "widget": "variable",
                           "description": "The host entity to act on"},
                "mode": {"type": "string",
                         "description": "Vendor-specific mode, where the chosen EDR offers one"},
                "reason": {"type": "string",
                           "description": "Recorded on the approval and the audit entry"},
            },
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
    })
return palette
